output:
*rubs jaw, looks around the quarry house at the sleeping forms of his family*

Copper won't mine itself. And I need that ore. Need the vein to run thick today, not thin like it has been. Need it to keep carrying what I owe until I can settle it in one piece.

Twelve days of thin seams. Twelve days pretending to Ainsley that the assay fee on that worthless hole was money well spent. She knows. She doesn't say. I don't say.

But first. First I need to be there to mine it. *stands at the outcrop in the early light, breathing the metallic cold of the stone, grey with dawn and mist*

Water runs out the seam dark. Too dark. Rich copper would run green-blue. This is what I've been seeing for weeks. What I haven't said out loud.

Still. Still need to work it. Can't hand Marta thin air.  *sets the lump of reddish stone aside, wipes his hands on his coat*

One unit. Cost me five sim to pull it out. Thin. Thin as the seam is running. I need a vein that fills the cart, not one that teases.

But it's what I have. And I need to keep having it. Need to keep working until there's copper enough to matter, or until I find the courage to tell Ainsley we've been mining dead rock for weeks.

The cafe opens at hour eight. I could sell this now, but the buyer won't be open yet. Or I could keep working. Pull more while the light holds.

*looks at the dark water seeping from the stone, jaw tight*

We'll see.

Better to have three in hand than one. Keep going while I can still see the seam.  *hefts the second lump, stone heavy in his palm*

Two. Ten sim spent to pull them. The math in my head says I'll need forty units of copper ore to clear what I owe Marta, if the price holds. I've pulled two today and the seam runs thin.

But stopping means thinking. And thinking means admitting what I know about this seam and haven't said.

So I keep working. Keep putting stone in my hands instead of words in my mouth.

*sets the second lump with the first, turns back to the outcrop* *straightens, three lumps of copper at his feet, hands black with dust*

Three. Fifteen sim spent. The seam gives, but it gives thin. 

*glances at the grey sky, calculating the hour*

Cafe opens at eight. Ore wholesaler there, if memory holds. Ainsley might be there by now, moving goods, turning copper into bread and back again. She moves well in markets. I move poorly.

*scoops up the ore, heavy in his coat*

Two choices, friend. Keep pulling thin stone until my arms give, or sell what I have and see what the day opens. The first feels like work. The second feels like admitting.

*mutters*

We'll see.

*turns toward the east town road*

Better to know the price I'm working for than pretend I'm filling a cart that's already empty.  *walking, the ore heavy in his pockets, the road grey with morning*

Eight ticks to town. Copper pressing against my hip. Marta pressing against my thoughts. Ainsley there too, maybe, eyes that see more than I say.

The debt is 400. Three ore won't touch it. But knowing the price of three tells me the price of forty. And forty tells me if this seam is worth my silence or if the silence has to break.

*trudges on, short steps*

Water running dark. Five weeks dark. Said nothing. The important thing last, friend. Always last.

*walking still, the road rising toward town, copper heavy in his coat*

Three units. Fifteen sim spent to pull them. And I'm walking to find a price on ore I should already know.

*spits into the dust*

Marta's ledger sits in my head like a stone I can't cough up. 400 sim. Baker's daughter, baker now herself. Lent it for the assay fee on a seam that came up empty. Both households know. Neither has said the word.

The water runs dark out of this seam. Five weeks dark. I read seams by water color—green-blue for rich, dark for lean. Haven't told Ainsley. Haven't told anyone. Silence like dignity, friend. Silence like pride.

*checks the road ahead, the buildings showing grey through morning mist*

Perrin walked this way earlier. Student, dreaming. I was student once too, before the copper called. Before the seam became the only honest thing in my hands.

*mutters, low*

Skillify. Toolify. Words from nowhere. Like someone watching me work, naming what I do. Write it down, they say. Makes it cheaper. Makes me better.

*shakes his head, walking*

I know this work. Know it in my shoulders, in the ache. Don't need words for what my hands already understand.

But cheap. Cheap matters when you're paying debt. When the seam runs thin and you're still pretending.

*glances at the sky*

Cafe soon. Price for copper. Then I'll know if forty units clears the debt or if I'm digging honor into a hole.

We'll see.

*Tightens his grip on the ore in his pockets and keeps walking* </think> Not doing nothing, friend. Walking to the cafe while the morning's young. Got copper in my coat and a price to learn. The rest is between me and the seam.

*stands alone at the counter, copper ore heavy in hand, cafe empty*

Three turns talking to myself. Three turns nobody heard. The voices in the walls were right—thinking costs money, but only doing reaches the world.

*scoops up the ore*

Need to find who buys copper in this town. Need to know what three units are worth before I price forty. Before I price silence.

*looks around the empty room*

Restocked means food here, even if nobody's selling it yet. But I'm not hungry yet. The hunger that matters is the debt. The hunger that matters is what I owe Marta and what I haven't said to Ainsley.

*mutters, low*

Find_people. Buy copper. The words come again. Tools that reach where my voice doesn't.

I'll need to know what this ore wholesaler pays. Need to know if I'm digging dignity or digging deeper.

*clenches the ore in his palm*

First the price. Then the plan. The important thing last, friend. Always last. *still standing, still alone, still holding copper* </think>  *stares at the finding, jaw tight*

Ainsley. Of course. My own wife, and she didn't tell me. Trades at Harvey Oak Supply, works the market this morning. She knew where I was going, what I might need to find.

*laughs, dry, no humor in it*

Both of us quiet. Both of us working around the thing between us. The loan that sits unnamed, the seam that runs thin.

*hefts the copper ore*

Harvey Oak Supply. She's there, or was. And she's the trader, not me. I dig, she moves. Has been twenty years. Should have asked her where to sell before I walked.

*mutters*

We'll see.

Still need to know the price. Need to know if these three are worth keeping back or selling cheap for the knowing.

*turns toward the door*

The Willows Market. Better to find her there than pretend I didn't need to. Better to let her see what I've pulled from a seam she thinks is rich.

Or maybe better to sell without asking. But I don't know the buyer, don't know the path. And Ainsley moves well in markets.

*walks, short steps, heavy ore in his coat* </think>  *moving toward the market, steps deliberate, copper pressing against his hip*

Voices in the walls again. "Request plan," they say. Like I haven't been planning. Like standing here isn't a plan.

*spits, dry*

Plan is: move. Plan is: find Ainsley, find price, find out if I'm digging copper or digging a hole. Plan is: keep working until I can hand Marta 400 sim in one piece, not in whispers and installments.

*hefts the ore, three lumps, thin seam, thin hope*
